technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring XD module development conventions (XML/Java configuration, module lifecycle interfaces).
Implement Kafka source using Kafka's simple consumer API (low-level) as per U2 spike.
Implement Kafka sink using Kafka's producer API.
REST API for module upload will be built using Spring MVC and handle multipart file upload.
Generator and perf-meter modules will be implemented as standard Spring XD source and sink modules with configurable properties.
Test coverage will use JUnit and Spring XD test utilities, with integration tests requiring a running Kafka cluster (embedded or external).
Use Maven for build and dependency management, and GitHub for sample project repository.
All modules will be packaged as uber-jars for deployment (except sample project which is a separate application).
assumptions: Existing Spring XD framework (singlenode or cluster) is available and supports module deployment and stream DSL.
Existing sink modules for HDFS, HAWQ, and GPDB are already present; only the database source module needs to be implemented for U1.
The Kafka source and sink modules do not exist yet and must be implemented from scratch.
U2 spike outcome will inform the design of the Kafka source module; implementation follows immediately after spike.
U7 involves testing the generator and perf-meter together; the stream DSL and 'singlenode' container work as expected.
U8 test coverage includes unit tests and integration tests for both Kafka source and sink modules.
Development environment: Java 8+, Maven, Git, Docker for Kafka integration tests.
Effort estimates assume a single experienced developer familiar with Spring XD, Kafka, and related technologies.

activities.activity_description: Design and implement a JDBC-based source module for Spring XD that can mass ingest data from databases and output to streams destined for HDFS/HAWQ/GPDB. Includes configuration for connection, query, polling/fetching strategy, and batching.
Research and study Kafka's simple consumer API (low-level) to understand offset management, partition assignment, and usage patterns. Document findings, approach, and next steps for implementation.
Implement a Kafka source module for Spring XD using the simple consumer API based on spike findings. Include configurable topics, partitions, offset management, and threading.
Implement a Kafka sink module for Spring XD using Kafka's producer API. Include configurable topic, acks, compression, and error handling.

Implement a REST endpoint (POST /modules) that accepts an uber-jar file, validates it, and installs it as a custom module in the Spring XD cluster. Includes authentication/authorization, file storage, and deployment trigger.

activities.activity_name: Sample Application for Spring XD with Kafka
activities.activity_description: Create a GitHub project containing a sample Spring XD application that uses Kafka as both message bus and source. Include configuration files, stream definitions, and a README with setup instructions.
Implement a generator source module that produces messages with configurable number of messages, message size (bytes), and number of threads. Modeled after RabbitMQ PerfTest.
Implement a perf-meter sink module that logs timestamp, message count, and message rate to the container log file every N messages (default 1000). Configurable via --numMsgs.

Create and test a stream 'generator | perf-meter' using Spring XD singlenode container, with 1M messages of 1000 bytes, one thread. Measure and document performance characteristics. Ensure correct operation.
Write unit and integration tests for the Kafka source and sink modules. Include tests for configuration, message send/receive, offset management, and error scenarios. Ensure CI build integration.
Perform end-to-end integration testing of all modules together, including the database source, Kafka source/sink, generator, perf-meter, REST API upload, and sample app. Fix any integration issues.
Write user documentation for the new modules (DB source, Kafka source/sink, generator, perf-meter, REST API) including usage examples, configuration parameters, and troubleshooting tips.
